summary: Timezone/DST fix (client_time + Europe/Lisbon fallback) verified end-to-end. 10/10 backend pytest tests pass. Frontend correctly sends client_time ISO string with offset on both start and end calls. Also discovered & fixed a missing route decorator for /api/time-entries/my-realtime-status.

minor.issue: Missing @api_router.get decorator caused endpoint to return 404 (FIXED by adding decorator at server.py line ~4351)

issues: Times rendered via new Date(iso).toLocaleTimeString('pt-PT') use BROWSER timezone, not forced Europe/Lisbon. For Portuguese users on correct device TZ this is fine, but displaying +01:00 ISO times in a UTC-browser (e.g., test env) shows 08:00 instead of 09:00. Consider passing { timeZone: 'Europe/Lisbon' } to toLocaleTimeString to ensure display correctness across devices.

action_items: [OPTIONAL] Harden display: pass { timeZone: 'Europe/Lisbon' } to all toLocaleTimeString calls in Dashboard.jsx / mobile views to render HH:MM consistently in Lisbon time regardless of device timezone.
[INFO] The missing decorator for /api/time-entries/my-realtime-status was fixed by the test agent.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py line 4351-4352: get_my_realtime_status was defined without @api_router.get('/time-entries/my-realtime-status'). Fixed during this run. Indicates a prior copy-paste error.
get_now_local/get_today_local/format_time_from_iso helpers (lines 486-540) are correctly implemented and used consistently in start/end/today/realtime-status endpoints.
models.py: TimeEntryStart and TimeEntryEnd correctly declare Optional[str] client_time field.
Frontend utils/timeUtils.js getLocalISOString() produces correct ISO with offset (verified: browser sent '2026-04-20T09:32:22+00:00' in UTC env, would send +01:00 in Portugal summer).
Backend start endpoint stores start_time EXACTLY as '2026-04-20T09:00:00+01:00' when client sends +01:00 offset (no UTC conversion) and derives date='2026-04-20' from local time (verified via GET).
seed_data_creation: Created several time_entries for user teste@email.com (observations prefixed TEST_*). Most were ended during tests; a couple completed entries remain in DB for date 2026-04-20.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Timezone fix is working. Key validation: POST /api/time-entries/start with client_time='2026-04-20T09:00:00+01:00' stores start_time='2026-04-20T09:00:00+01:00' (NOT UTC 08:00) and date='2026-04-20'. End endpoint computes total_hours correctly across timezone offsets (e.g., 09:00+01:00 → 17:00+01:00 = 8.0h). /api/time-entries/today filters by LOCAL date, not UTC. /api/admin/realtime-status and /api/time-entries/my-realtime-status use format_time_from_iso which converts stored ISO to Europe/Lisbon for HH:MM display. Fallback (no client_time) correctly uses Europe/Lisbon now(). NOTE: One issue was discovered and fixed by the test agent: get_my_realtime_status had no route decorator (returned 404); added @api_router.get('/time-entries/my-realtime-status').
rca of the issue: Original bug: all time-entry code used datetime.now(timezone.utc) → during Portugal summer (UTC+1) a 09:00 local event was stored as 08:00 UTC and its 'date' was derived from UTC (could even be previous day near midnight). Fix: introduced get_now_local(client_time_str) which parses ISO with offset from client or falls back to Europe/Lisbon. All start/end/today/realtime endpoints use these helpers; format_time_from_iso converts stored ISO to Lisbon TZ for HH:MM display. Secondary bug found by tests: the my-realtime-status function lacked a route decorator (404). Fixed by adding @api_router.get('/time-entries/my-realtime-status').
